bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to the authority of Congress and the States to regulate contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections and to enact public financing systems for political campaigns.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The amendment would reshape campaign finance law, directly affecting lobbying firms and attorneys who advise on election spending and compliance.
Advocacy organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new regulatory authority over their fundraising and expenditures.
Regulations on election spending could affect advertising revenue and the market for political communications services.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit them to create public financing systems for campaigns and to treat corporations differently from individual people, including by prohibiting corporations from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

bill.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared with respect to energy.
bill.latestActionText: Failed of passage in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 47 - 51. Record Vote Number: 554.

industries.rationale: The emergency declaration explicitly expedites approvals for oil, gas, and coal development and infrastructure, which this resolution would terminate.
The emergency order covers renewable energy resources and infrastructure, so ending it would affect expedited permitting for solar, wind, and storage projects.
The emergency declaration addresses energy infrastructure and supply adequacy, directly affecting utilities' ability to build transmission and generation facilities under expedited timelines.
The emergency order includes critical minerals and uranium in its definition of energy resources subject to expedited development.
The emergency invokes military construction authority and expedites energy infrastructure projects, affecting contractors who build pipelines, power plants, and related facilities.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would end the national energy emergency that the President declared in January 2025. That emergency declaration directed federal agencies to speed up approvals for energy projects—including oil, gas, coal, renewables, and infrastructure like pipelines—and gave the Defense Department authority to use emergency construction powers to address energy supply vulnerabilities. Terminating the emergency would remove those expedited authorities and return permitting and development processes to their standard procedures.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys fuel or heats a home. People who live near a mine, and people who work in one.

bill.latestActionText: Motion to proceed to consideration of measure rejected in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 43 - 50. Record Vote Number: 4.
subjects: Wilderness and natural areas, wildlife refuges, wild rivers, habitats

industries.rationale: Regional haze rules typically impose emissions controls on coal-fired power plants and other fossil-fuel facilities that contribute to visibility impairment.
Electric utilities operating in South Dakota would be subject to the state implementation plan's requirements for reducing haze-causing emissions.
Industrial facilities that emit pollutants contributing to regional haze may face compliance obligations under the state plan.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn an Environmental Protection Agency rule that approved South Dakota's plan to reduce haze and improve visibility in national parks and wilderness areas. If passed, the resolution would nullify the EPA's approval of South Dakota's second-phase regional haze implementation plan, which was published in August 2025. The resolution uses the Congressional Review Act, a tool that allows Congress to reject recently issued federal regulations.

industries.rationale: The bill creates a new Medicare payment stream for ground ambulance services that do not result in transport, directly affecting ambulance operators' revenues and service models.
Medicare payment policy changes for emergency medical services affect the program's costs and may influence private insurers' coverage decisions for similar services.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs Medicare to test a five-year program that would pay ambulance services even when they respond to an emergency call but do not transport the patient to a hospital. Payment rates would generally match what Medicare currently pays when a patient is transported. The Government Accountability Office would study how the program affects Medicare beneficiaries' access to emergency medical services and their health outcomes.

bill.title: ABC Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: Streamlined administrative processes for Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP may affect how providers interact with patients' caregivers and handle eligibility documentation.
Changes to Medicare and Medicaid administrative processes could affect insurers participating in these programs and their coordination with caregivers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs federal agencies to review and simplify the paperwork and application processes for Medicare, Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program, and Social Security. The goal is to reduce the burden on family caregivers by eliminating duplicative forms and streamlining eligibility procedures across these programs. Agencies must gather input from caregivers and state organizations, make improvements, and report their progress to Congress.

bill.title: Save Our Seas 2.0 Amendments Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-65.
subjects: Social work, volunteer service, charitable organizations

industries.rationale: The bill funds programs that address marine debris and pollution, directly affecting waste management and water quality operations.
Marine debris affects navigation safety, which impacts shipping and maritime logistics operations.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends funding for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's Marine Debris Program through 2029 and reauthorizes the Marine Debris Foundation through 2025. It allows NOAA to contribute to marine debris cleanup projects using in-kind support and gives the foundation's board authority to hire and fire a chief executive officer. The bill also requires the foundation to develop outreach practices for Indian tribes and permits it to accept matching contributions from regional organizations, tribes, and foreign governments.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who drinks tap water.

bill.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose duties on articles imported from Canada.
bill.latestActionText: Held at the desk.
subjects: Presidents and presidential powers, Vice Presidents

industries.rationale: The resolution directly affects the 10% tariff on Canadian energy and energy resources.
The 25% tariff on most Canadian imports affects manufacturers who source materials, components, or finished goods from Canada.
Retailers importing consumer goods from Canada face the 25% tariff that this resolution would eliminate.
Agricultural products and food imports from Canada are subject to the 25% tariff.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would end the national emergency that President Trump declared on February 1, 2025, which imposed a 25% tariff on most goods imported from Canada and a 10% tariff on Canadian energy imports. Terminating the emergency would remove the legal basis for these additional duties on Canadian products.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys imported goods, and people who make goods here.

bill.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 461.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

industries.rationale: The bill directly funds research and development of drugs and therapies for ALS and neurodegenerative diseases, affecting pharmaceutical and biotech companies developing these treatments.
Clinical trial enrollment requirements and expanded access to investigational drugs may affect hospitals and health systems conducting ALS research and treatment.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal programs that support research and development of treatments for ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease) and similar neurodegenerative diseases. It requires the National Institutes of Health to track safety data more closely when awarding grants for experimental drug studies, and directs the Food and Drug Administration to publish five-year plans describing how it will help develop and approve treatments for these rare diseases. The bill also mandates reports evaluating the effectiveness of these grant programs.

plain.whoItTouches: People with an illness that is still being studied. Anyone who uses the internet.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
